Exhibit C TENANT DESIGN CRITERIA Nashville Farmers Market MARKET DESIGN CONCEPT The Nashville Farmers Market has remodeled the interior of the Market’s main building. This project will require all merchants to submit design packages that conform to the following rules. Each Tenant Design package will be reviewed by the Market Board of Directors, the Market Director and where necessary, the State of Tennessee. In addition, the Tenant’s plans must be approved by all the required agencies that review plans in Davidson County. Each shop will be reviewed both independently and how it interacts with the shops surrounding it. Tenants are encouraged to develop bold and creative shop designs within a set framework that ensures a lively, almost entertaining atmosphere, but within the overall design of the Market. Shops should allow open and clear contact between the merchant and customer and generous and attractive display of all products. Designs that feature the production of a specific product are encouraged. Much of the visual excitement of the Market depends on the openness of each stand allowing simultaneous intimate and long views of the Market as a whole. Each shop must be laid out so that it is both an attractive statement in itself, but also a window that provides views to the Market that lay beyond that particular shop. The Markets goal is the effective display of the full range of merchandise, without clutter and confusion, while maintaining easy but secure access for both customer and merchant. The character of each shop should reinforce the basic product group it offers. A good design allows the merchandise to speak for itself, with customer sight-lines to product production if possible. This will increase the customer’s interest in the merchant’s product and a sense of excitement. Only durable design and materials which will hold up under the usage experienced over the long term will be approved. Like any business investment, the shop should be seen as a capital asset that will retain its value only when planned and properly maintained. The optimum balance in the Market derives from individual shops that provide unity to the site as a whole while remaining unique in themselves. Compatibility with adjacent counters, signage and presentation must be taken into consideration and will be reviewed during the approval process. Architectural Systems Exterior building shell: Any modifications (new wall openings, roof penetrations, etc.) are subject to approval by the Market, and shall receive proper structural support and flashing for watertight performance. Architectural “trellis”: An overhead “trellis” frame is intended to be utilized for distribution of water piping and power conduit in open areas. (See Market standard drawings.) Tenant partitions: Wood or metal stud with gypsum wallboard, 12 feet high maximum. Architectural finishes: Materials within food preparation areas shall be impervious and scrubbable. Paint and stain shall be low-VOC formula. Any ceilings (optional) shall be subject to Market approval. Structural considerations: Kitchen cooking exhaust hoods and make-up air units must be supported by an independent frame that transfers weight to the overhead “trellis” or the floor slab. (Suspension from roof trusses is not permitted.) Support design shall be reviewed by a professional structural engineer. Mechanical and Electrical Systems Water: Service will be available from a point directed by the Market. (Metro Water Services may require a supplemental Tenant backflow-preventer under special conditions.) Water heaters shall be electric except where gas is acceptable to the Market. Venting of plumbing fixtures may be “Studor”-type. Sewer / Grease: Sinks and floor drains shall be drained to primary under-slab sewer network (see Market standard drawings). (Supplemental in-line grease-traps may be utilized only in special cases where acceptable to Codes officials and the Market.) Piping vents in interior building zones shall be special interior-venting type unless otherwise required by Metro Plumbing Codes. Natural gas: Service will be available from a point directed by the Market. Tenant meter shall be placed as directed by the Market. Venting of gas-fired equipment shall be in accordance with established building standards. Heating/ventilation/cooling: Tenants are advised that enclosing spaces from the common building environment may cause air-flow stagnation in Tenant space; any supplemental cooling will be the Tenant’s responsibility. Placement of exterior condensers-compressors for food-service equipment is subject to Market approval. Cooking hoods: Design and construction shall comply with currently-enforced editions of NFPA 96 and SMC Chapter 5 (a checklist for which is available from the Tennessee Fire Marshal’s office), as well as Market standard hood specifications. Placement of cooking hoods and conditioned makeup-air equipment, and routing of exhaust ductwork shall be controlled as shown on Market standard drawings. Fire detection and suppression: Cooking hoods shall be connected to building fire-alarm system as directed by the Market. Any modification of building fire-sprinkler system to accommodate ceilings or other obstructions shall be distributed from overhead trellis. Electrical Power: Service connection will be available from a point directed by the Market. Tenant meter shall be placed as directed by the Market. Farmers Market Tenant Design Criteria 2 of 6 ARCHIVE
Lighting: Illumination intensity is subject to Market approval. Architectural Design Design Control Zones: Shop layout shall provide maximum open display frontage along the public perimeter. The following four Design Zones (measured vertically from the floor) have been established: Lower Display Zone (from the floor to 42” above the floor / with specific approval up to 56” above the floor): All approved display fixtures and equipment are allowed. Public aisle frontage must be used for product display or service activity, except for access openings. Goods within display cases should be maintained as presentation instead of storage. Upper Display Zone: There are two subdivisions within this zone. Perimeter Upper Display Zone (from lease-line to 42” in from the lease-line or column line): No fixtures or equipment allowed except approved refrigerated display equipment. Interior Upper Display Zone (remainder of Upper Display Zone, excluding Perimeter Upper Display Zone): Signage Zone (from 108” to 144” above the floor): See section on signage. Restricted Zone (more than 144” above the floor): Awnings, canopies, and ceilings are prohibited in this zone or anywhere else. Architectural “trellis”: Tenants are responsible for constructing an overhead structure and valance along the public perimeter, from which water and power is to be distributed, from which tenant lighting (and ceilings, if applicable) are to be suspended, and on which Tenant signage shall be mounted. (See Market Standard Drawings.) Architectural finishes: Materials shall be limited to the following. Flooring: Stained concrete, or hard tile (ceramic, stone, clay), epoxy resinous topping, with slip- resistant surface. A smooth, durable, cleanable base (no wood, wood-composite, non-factory painted material) is required up to 4” above the floor. Raised areas may be permitted on a case-by-case basis. Vertical surfaces: Hard tile (ceramic, stone, clay), glass, stainless steel, finished solid wood siding (only in non-food areas). Provide metal corner guards at aisle intersections. Horizontal surfaces: Stainless steel, natural butcher block, hard tile (ceramic, stone, clay), polyethylene cutting board, glass, marble or granite, solid resin (corian or equivalent). Ceilings (to be constructed only where mandated by health regulations): Tile. Exposed particleboard, plywood and plywood paneling are prohibited anywhere in public view. Plastic laminates are not permitted and may not be used in work area countertops or in high wear or high visibility areas. Paint and stain shall be low-VOC formula. Window Treatments: Tenants located against an exterior window must maintain those windows as presentation areas for their shop and the Market as a whole. Unsightly uses such as storage are not permitted at windows. Utility Systems Cooking-hoods: Placement of cooking-hoods and routing of exhaust ductwork shall be restricted as shown on Market Standard Drawings. Supplemental conditioned make-up air for cooking-hoods shall be provided, via operable exterior thru-wall louvers placed as a location to be determined by Landlord’s engineers. Fire suppression system within each hood will be integrated into Market fire alarm system. Water: Secondary services will be extended from primary to readily accessible points on the overhead trellis. Distribution is to be from overhead trellis and within demising partitions. (Metro Water Services may require supplemental backflow-prevention under special conditions.) Farmers Market Tenant Design Criteria 3 of 6 ARCHIVE
Sewer: Non-grease-collecting sinks and floor drains may be tied directly into building sanitary line. Sinks in interior zones must be special self-venting type. Placement of floor drains must accommodate positive drainage. Grease filtration / tenants: A 2,700 gallon grease interceptor has been installed. Each Tenant must have an in-line grease-traps (by tenants) which will be utilized to remove grease prior to entering the primary sewer. (Note: This strategy is subject to limitation based on customer load.) Natural gas: Distribution is to be from overhead trellis and within partitions. Fire suppression: Modification of building sprinkler system to accommodate new ceilings is to be distributed from overhead trellis. Electrical Power: Secondary services will be extended from primary to readily accessible points on the overhead trellis. Distribution is to be from overhead trellis and within partitions. Prior to final approval of electrical installation, Tenant shall notify Landlord who will then have a electrical meter installed. Lighting Tenant space illumination levels are subject to Market approval. Light sources generating glare in the common area are not allowed; provide special baffles or diffusers to shield lamps from direct view at eye- level. Light color is to simulate natural daylight so far as practicable; fluorescent lamps shall be deluxe warm-white, General illumination may be used in task areas; accent lighting is encouraged within primary and secondary Display Zones. (Animated or flashing fixtures are not permitted.) Signage Permanent: At least one permanent sign shall be required per stall, located within the Signage Zone. Two types of permanent signage are permitted, all limited to the Signage Zone: Within and parallel to the lease-line: Maximum 8 square-feet on large frontages, or 6 square-feet on smaller frontages. Projecting from the lease-line: Maximum | per tenant and not to exceed 4 square-feet and cannot exceed 3 linear feet in any one dimension. Tenants against an exterior window: Maximum one per window and maximum 4 square feet, mounted on a transparent panel and hung with metal cable. Signs shall contain only the store name and logo, or a design representing the goods or services offered for sale. Listing of merchandise or services will not be permitted unless it is part of the name. Pictographic, carved, neon and similar specialty signage types are encouraged. (Animated component, flashing light, fabric, canvas, formed plastic, backlit glass, plexiglass or injection-molded signs are not permitted.) Temporary: Signs for special announcements, daily or seasonal items are permitted under these conditions: They are for truly temporary purposes -- not as a substitute for permanent signage or menu board. They are located within the primary or secondary Display Zones. They are not attached to the permanent sign or menu board. They do not exceed 100 square-inches, and are made of card stock or better material They are clean and orderly. Acoustics The Market reserves the right to reject equipment that generates unusual noise levels. Security A graphic curtain or gate may be utilized as security barrier. Blue tarps will not be permitted. Storage Experience indicates that storage needs are frequently underestimated and can interfere with efficient operations if not properly accommodated in the initial design. Two general storage strategies are permitted: Farmers Market Tenant Design Criteria 4 of 6 ARCHIVE
In shop: Must be enclosed by cabinets Remote: Within designated areas in the Market and leased to and maintained by the Tenant for that purpose. Dry or refrigerated space is available on a first-come/first-serve basis. In all areas appropriate capacity should be carefully determined so that orderliness is maintained. Designated storage areas must appear on the design drawings and will be reviewed for approval during the design process. TENANT APPROVAL PROCESS Each shop will be designed by the Tenant, and is subject to the following approval process directed by the Market Director. The Market Board of Directors will approve the Design and Construction Documents, and both Metro and Tennessee governments will have the option of reviewing the Documents. Because of the uniqueness of the designs and specific locations, the Market Board of Directors may make an exception to the Design Criteria for one merchant without allowing any other exception of a similar kind. Tenant submissions and approvals will be required for the following three phases. The following Documents must be submitted for review and approval by the Market Reviewers. Design Documents Narrative description (1 page) of shop design and materials, including merchandising strategy and how these complement the general character and function of the Market. Drawings at 1/4” = 10” scale describing the essential components of each discipline: Architectural: Floor plan, elevations of aisle frontages, interior construction Structural: Supplemental trellis, valance, etc. Plumbing: Fixtures (with graphic product sheets) Mechanical: Cooking hoods (with graphic product sheets) Electrical and Lighting (with graphic product sheets) Samples of key materials such as tile and countertop Construction Documents Following approval of Design Documents, submit detailed Construction Documents for all disciplines, before being submitted for approvals by State and Metro codes authorities. Additional Construction Documents (CDs) required include: Shop drawing of valance signage at 3” = 1’ scale Specifications for all materials Construction Before construction can begin, the following Documents must be submitted to the Market Director: A final set of Construction Documents, with applicable permits and approvals of codes authorities affixed Certificates of Insurance from all trades A recordable waiver of liens (or bond in lieu thereof) from the General Contractor in the amount of the construction contract sum The names and addresses of all contractors and subcontractors intended to be utilized by the Tenant Contractors must be licensed and approved by the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County. The Tenant shall not employ personnel unqualified for the work being performed. Construction activities shall be coordinated so as to minimize interference with existing tenants. Dust barriers and special work hours may be required, as requested by the Market. The Market Director reserves the right to demand modifications of Tenant construction in the event that constructed conditions do not comply with approved Design Documents. Farmers Market Tenant Design Criteria 5 of 6 ARCHIVE
Timeliness of Submittals Ina construction project of this magnitude and with this large a group of participants, timeliness is imperative. If one party does not provide the needed document or piece of equipment when required, it can set the whole project back. Because the Farmers Market and other tenants are depending on each participant to perform on a timely basis, we will have to require monetary damages if someone does not deliver the required information or product by the date it is due. Each Tenant will receive a written timetable on when each item is due. If the item is not received within 3 days after the due date, the monetary damages will begin. Those damages will be $100.00 per day for the first seven days, after that it will be $500.00 per day. If the delay extends beyond 30 days, then the Lessor may terminate the lease agreement with the Lessee. The Lessor will deliver a written document to the Lessee stating that the lease is hereby terminated and Lessor may collect any additional damages. Addendum: The separate Kitchen Hood and Fire Protection System Criteria shall become a part of the Tenant Design Criteria for all merchants within the Farmer’s Market that will require a hood system. Farmers Market Tenant Design Criteria 6 of 6 ARCHIVE
